newsitem.title: EGYPT: Egyptian mission depends on progress - ambassador.
newsitem.headline: Egyptian mission depends on progress - ambassador.

text.p: An Egyptian mediation mission to Israel and the Palestinian territories next week depends on progress through ordinary diplomatic channels, the Egyptian ambassador to Israel said on Friday.
Ambassador Mohammad Bassiouny told reporters that Egyptian envoy Osama el-Baz still planned to make the trip and would fix the dates to suit the Israelis and Palestinians.
"This trip is subject to achieving some kind of progress through ordinary diplomatic channels," he added.

Egypt is leading an attempt to revive substantial talks between the two sides, which have held few meetings since Israel decided in March to go ahead with building a Jewish settlement at Har Homa or Jabal Abu Ghneim in Arab East Jerusalem.

It says it is seeking a formula under which Israel would suspend settlement activity in occupied territories for long enough to persuade the Palestinians to resume the talks. The Israeli government has refused to give such a pledge.

"The gap is still very big between the Israeli and Palestinian sides because of the question of settlements in general and Jabal Abu Ghneim in particular. We hope Egyptian efforts will be able to find a formula which helps remove the reasons which led to the halt in talks," said Bassiouny.
The ambassador was speaking at Cairo airport at the start of a short visit home to brief Foreign Minister Amr Moussa.
Moussa said in Jordan on Tuesday that Arab-Israeli peace negotiations had reached their lowest point in 20 years.
On Friday Israeli soldiers shot and wounded at least seven Palestinians during clashes with Arab demonstrators in the divided West Bank town of Hebron, witnesses said.

They said about 50 Palestinian youths took part in the clashes, hurling dozens of fire bombs and home-made stun bombs of baking soda and water at soldiers across the invisible line that divides Hebron into Israeli- and PLO-controlled zones.
